title: LP2-49–51: missing-prime shuffle controls
question: Is the count of three absent decimal-prime values unusual under two fixed first-digit shuffle controls?
summary: Three absent values occurred in 761/5,000 global and 763/5,000 within-row shuffled grids. The missing-count pattern is not rare under these two controls.

scope.representation: First characters of 256 case-preserved grid tokens in the original 32x8 page-row order.
scope.procedure: Apply the fixed 1,364 directed four-cell path and decimal-prime rule to the observed grid and to 5,000 global plus 5,000 within-row digit shuffles.
scope.parameters: Seed 33012026; preserve global first-digit counts or each row composition; four predeclared statistics; 49-value prime universe; plus-one empirical tails.
scope.exclusions: No alternative path rule, suffix reading, text decryption, test of the specific three named omissions, correction for prior pattern search, or claim about authorship.

finding: The claim that three missing values alone is unusual is not supported under either declared shuffle model: >=3 omissions occurred in 15.24% and 15.28% of the plus-one empirical comparisons.
limitations: Exploratory control planned after observing the three absent values. Conditional shuffles do not model all plausible construction processes; a different predeclared statistic could behave differently. Human review pending.
next_steps: Test independently predicted features with a held-out or preregistered rule; keep any layout, path-length or null-model change as a linked variant.
